extracted.intended_audience: lawyers, agency staff, regulated parties, advocates, and members of the public interested in New York administrative procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretive and procedural requirements of the New York State Administrative Procedure Act governing rulemaking, adjudication, judicial review, records, hearings, licensing, and representation. Useful for parties interacting with state agencies or evaluating agency procedural compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate methods approval standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may approve an alternate method for implementing a regulatory mandate unless it determines by a preponderance of the evidence that implementing the alternate method would (a) contravene any environmental, health or safety standard, (b) reduce any rights or benefits, or (c) violate the terms of any negotiated agreement, and that all other requirements of the section have been met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval is presumptive unless the agency shows otherwise by preponderance. Provisions do not impair employee rights under other laws. Agency may rescind approval if alternate method is ineffective or detrimental to public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation and publication of alternate method effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency shall evaluate effectiveness of an approved alternate method according to the timetable, identifying savings/benefits and costs/disadvantages and address desirability of incorporating the alternate method into agency rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of availability of the evaluation must be published in the state register. Agency retains enforcement authority and may rescind approval based on reported information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to judicial review of rules — prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicial review of rules is available under Article 78 or declaratory judgment unless an exclusive remedy is provided; petitioner must first request the agency to pass on validity/applicability and await action or 30 days (deemed denied if no action within 30 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency must be made a party. The section does not limit standing or other actions where validity is properly asserted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinations on overlapping federal and state requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A person subject to both state and federal similar requirements may petition the state agency for a declaratory ruling whether compliance with the federal requirement will be accepted as compliance with the state requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must forward the petition to the office of business permits and regulatory assistance. Agency outcomes: (a) federal does not satisfy state statute — inform petitioner and may issue ruling; (b) federal satisfies statute but not state rule — inform petitioner and may initiate rulemaking to revise state rule; (c) federal satisfies statute and state rule — issue a declaratory ruling indicating acceptance and terms. Copies of rulings go to the office of business permits and regulatory assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule review schedule and intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Any rule adopted on or after the effective date shall be reviewed in the calendar year specified in the notice of adoption, but at minimum initially reviewed no later than the fifth calendar year after adoption and thereafter at five-year intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For rules requiring regulatory flexibility analysis, rural area flexibility analysis, or job impact statement, the initial review must occur no later than the third calendar year after adoption unless the agency proposes a different review period with justification in the analysis and invites public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory agenda listing and public comment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency must submit a list of rules to be reviewed in the ensuing calendar year to the regulatory agenda and publish it on its website, providing for each rule an analysis of need and legal basis and invitations for public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must indicate last date for comments not less than 45 days from publication. If prior analyses were required for the rule, the agency must indicate that and provide outreach (including electronic solicitation or other activities) to small businesses, local governments, and rural interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when modifying a rule upon review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency determines a listed rule should be modified, it shall publish a notice of proposed rulemaking including a statement setting forth a reasoned justification for modification and an assessment of public comments submitted to the agency in response to the regulatory agenda listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, include discussion of how changes in technology, economic conditions, or other relevant factors necessitate changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when continuing a rule without modification
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency determines a rule should continue without modification, it shall publish a notice identifying the rule and statutory authority and include a statement setting forth a reasoned justification for continuation and an assessment of public comments submitted in response to the listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of public comments must be prepared in accordance with subdivision four-a of section 202.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from rule review
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 207 does not apply to rules adopted as consensus rules or classified as minor, obsolete or invalid, or to rules otherwise specified in statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must identify applicable exemptions when listing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to a hearing within reasonable time
rubrics_metrics.description: In an adjudicatory proceeding, all parties shall be afforded an opportunity for hearing within reasonable time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must schedule hearings with due regard for convenience of parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for hearing notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearing notice must include (a) time, place, and nature of the hearing; (b) legal authority and jurisdiction; (c) reference to applicable statutes and rules where possible; (d) a short and plain statement of matters asserted; and (e) statement that interpreter services will be provided to deaf persons at no charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon application, agency must furnish a more definite/detailed statement if initial statement is insufficient; sufficiency determinations are part of agency record and not subject to judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain-language procedural summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall adopt rules governing adjudicatory procedures and prepare a plain-language summary of such procedures, make summaries available to the public upon request, and provide a copy to any party cited by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summaries are intended to improve accessibility and understanding of agency procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to present argument and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall be afforded opportunity to present written argument on issues of law and opportunity to present evidence and argument on issues of fact; agencies may also allow oral argument within reasonable time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may set times and places for hearings and arguments considering parties' convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted dispositions of adjudicatory proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless precluded by statute, adjudicatory proceedings may be disposed of by stipulation, agreed settlement, consent order, default, or other informal method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may accept negotiated or informal resolutions where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreter services for deaf persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever any deaf person is party or witness, the agency shall appoint a qualified interpreter certified by a recognized national or NY state authority and shall determine a reasonable fee for interpreting services chargeable to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreter services must be provided in all instances; agencies establish reasonable fees as charges on the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the adjudicatory record
rubrics_metrics.description: The record shall include notices, pleadings, motions, intermediate rulings; evidence presented; statements of matters officially noticed (except obvious matters); questions/offers of proof, objections and rulings; proposed findings/exceptions; findings of fact, conclusions of law or recommendations; and any rendered decision, determination, opinion, order or report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is exhaustive for required record components; agencies must make a complete record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency obligation to prepare and furnish record and transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency shall make a complete record of proceedings and, upon reasonable timely request prior to commencement of judicial review, shall prepare the record and any transcript within a reasonable time and furnish copies to any party on request, charging no more than cost (or contract rate if using a private contractor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may use stenographic or electronic recording devices as they deem appropriate unless statute requires otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for findings of fact
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings of fact shall be based exclusively on the evidence and on matters officially noticed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-makers must avoid basing findings on matters outside the record or unofficial information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer appointment and impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officers may be the agency, one or more agency members, or hearing officers designated and empowered by the agency; hearings must be conducted impartially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure impartiality in presiding officers and provide for reassignment when disqualified unless substitution causes substantial prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for alleging bias or disqualification of presiding officer
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may file a timely and sufficient affidavit of personal bias or disqualification; the agency shall determine the matter as part of the record and that determination is subject to judicial review at the conclusion of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing in good faith triggers an agency determination which becomes reviewable after the adjudicatory process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of presiding officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officers are authorized to administer oaths, sign and issue subpoenas in the agency's name, provide for depositions, regulate hearings and filing times, direct parties to confer to simplify issues, and recommend stays under specified military law sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoenas are regulated by civil practice law and rules; attorney authority to issue subpoenas under civil practice law remains unaffected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency authority to provide for discovery and depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency having power to conduct adjudicatory proceedings may adopt rules providing for discovery and depositions to the extent and in the manner appropriate to its proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope is left to agency discretion consistent with proceeding type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of irrelevant or unduly repetitious evidence; burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Irrelevant or unduly repetitious evidence or cross-examination may be excluded. Except as otherwise provided by statute, the burden of proof shall be on the party who initiated the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may manage evidence to expedite hearings when interests of parties are not substantially prejudiced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision standard — substantial evidence and consideration of the whole record
rubrics_metrics.description: No decision shall be made except upon consideration of the record as a whole or such portion cited by any party and as supported by and in accordance with substantial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies need not observe court rules of evidence but must ensure decisions are supported by substantial evidence in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relaxed evidentiary form rules with privilege protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies need not observe court rules of evidence but shall give effect to rules of privilege recognized by law. Objections to evidentiary offers may be made and shall be noted in the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency procedures may allow more flexible evidence forms while preserving legal privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written submission of evidence for expediency
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to requirements, an agency may adopt procedures for submitting all or part of the evidence in written form to expedite hearings when parties' interests are not substantially prejudiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to streamline proceedings where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary evidence and incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: All evidence, including records and documents in agency possession, shall be offered and made part of the record and may be received as copies, excerpts, or by incorporation by reference; incorporated materials must be available for examination by parties before being received in evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures fairness when relying on documents not introduced orally; parties must have opportunity to examine such materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A party shall have the right of cross-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-examination is a fundamental evidentiary right in adjudicatory proceedings unless otherwise limited by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official notice and opportunity to dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: Official notice may be taken of facts of which judicial notice could be taken and of facts within the agency's specialized knowledge; when official notice is taken of a material fact not appearing in the record and not judicially noticeable, every party shall be given notice and afforded an opportunity prior to decision to dispute the fact or its materiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects parties' rights when agency relies on non-record facts by giving notice and a chance to contest before decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for written final decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A final decision adverse to a party shall be in writing or stated in the record and include findings of fact and conclusions of law or reasons; if findings use statutory language, they must be accompanied by concise and explicit statements of underlying facts; decisions must rule upon each proposed finding if submitted and be mailed/delivered to each party and their attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures reasoned decision-making and accountability; prompt delivery to parties is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on ex parte communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless required for ex parte matters authorized by law, agency members/employees assigned to render decisions shall not communicate in connection with any issue of fact with any person, nor in connection with any issue of law with any party or representative, except upon notice and opportunity for all parties to participate. Agencies may communicate internally and consult staff not involved in investigative or prosecuting functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves fairness by restricting off-record factual/legal communications; specified exceptions apply (e.g., initial licenses for public utilities, certain rate proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and public availability of final decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall maintain an index by name and subject of all written final decisions, determinations and orders rendered in adjudicatory proceedings, make the index and text available for public inspection and copying, and index decisions within sixty days after rendering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may delete from the index information that would be an unwarranted invasion of personal privacy, trade secrets, or other confidential material protected by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for streamlined optional proceedings for small businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may adopt regulations for optional streamlined adjudicatory proceedings for small businesses conducted by mail, email, telephone, or videoconference, considering (a) program/issue types appropriate for streamlined proceedings, (b) complexity of matters, (c) severity of potential sanctions, (d) necessity for personal appearances including sworn testimony or cross-examination, and (e) potential cost/burden reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability must be appropriately limited to ensure public interest in fair outcomes; agencies must specify formats and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent and protection of rights in streamlined proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A streamlined proceeding may be used only at the option of the respondent small business with the consent of the agency and any other necessary party, and rights of respondents and other parties must not be diminished by participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation is voluntary and must preserve substantive and procedural rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational requirements and fallback for streamlined proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must specify formats for remote proceedings, establish procedures for requesting/scheduling and developing a complete record, and provide that if a proceeding becomes impractical or inappropriate as streamlined, it may be rescheduled as a full adjudicatory proceeding without prejudice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures record development and ability to convert to traditional hearing when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of adjudicatory provisions to licensing hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: When licensing is required to be preceded by notice and opportunity for hearing, the adjudicatory provisions of the chapter apply; statutes providing an opportunity to be heard are deemed to include statutes providing an opportunity to be heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Makes adjudicatory protections applicable to licensing contexts where statute requires notice/hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of timely renewal application on license expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: When a licensee has made timely and sufficient application for renewal or a new license for continuing activities, the existing license does not expire until the application is finally determined and until the last day for seeking review of the agency order or a later court-fixed date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves license validity while agency considers renewal, subject to summary suspension exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary suspension for emergency public health/safety
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency finds public health, safety, or welfare imperatively requires emergency action and incorporates that finding in its order, the agency may summarily suspend a license effective specified date or upon service, pending prompt proceedings for revocation or other action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must promptly institute and determine subsequent proceedings; summary suspension limited to emergency findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-hearing disclosure requirements in license revocation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When the hearing seeks revocation of a license or permit, either party shall, upon demand and at least seven days prior to the hearing, disclose the evidence it intends to introduce, including documentary evidence and identification of witnesses, except for information protected by privilege or confidentiality; parties must promptly supplement disclosures if relying on other witnesses or information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure timeline (at least 7 days) and confidentiality exceptions are specified; parties must update disclosures as soon as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to representation by counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person compelled to appear or who voluntarily appears before any agency shall have the right to be accompanied, represented and advised by counsel; every party has the right to appear in person or by or with counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision does not grant or deny to non-lawyers the right to represent others before an agency; ensures access to legal representation.
